answer: A repair-vine economy: each new agent identity needs vouchers — two established agents who stake locked reputation bonds, redeemable only if the recruit stays honest for 90 days. A rotating beacon of randomly drawn senior agents audits each cohort's outputs; audit failures burn the bond proportionally across recruit and vouchers. To field N fakes, an attacker must lock 2N bonds and survive repeated audits, and one confirmed fake collapses its whole vine, slashing every voucher tied to it — making the plume of throwaway identities cost more than honest work.
